ai_break_stance.de_rate_prices_the_break: partially - the de-rate prices the cycle HOLDING (the disruption case), so a break is upside not downside
ai_break_stance.explicit: ADBE is the rare INVERSE. The bear case requires venture/hyperscaler-subsidised generative competitors (Sora, Midjourney, Runway, Canva, Figma) to keep offering near-free model-native creation - that subsidy is capital-cycle-funded. A capex break de-funds the challenger cohort, forces inference to price at cost, and leaves Adobe's enterprise contracts, IP-indemnified corpus and distribution intact. Adobe carries almost NO AI capex of its own: FY25 PP&E capex $179M on $23.77B revenue = 0.75%, so no depreciation cliff and no stranded compute. With the household already ~$5.2M/26% long the cycle holding, ADBE is a structurally scarce fundamental offset. CAVEAT, not averaged away: in the first weeks of a break correlations go to one and ADBE sells with everything; the negative beta here is FUNDAMENTAL, not price-path. This is an 18-month hedge, not a two-week one.

honesty_finding.masking_channel: acquired-ARR substitution inside an unchanged headline growth target, plus segment retirement and base revaluation
honesty_finding.signal_channel: organic net-new ARR increments (the leading indicator); revenue/EPS are lagging
honesty_finding.signal_to_price_latency: 1-2 quarters - the ARR book converts to revenue with a lag, so the organic deceleration reaches the printed revenue line around Q1-Q2 FY27
honesty_finding.detail: FY26 'Total Adobe ending ARR growth' target was 10.2% in the Q4 FY25 release (2025-12-10) EXPLICITLY excluding Semrush ('do not include any contributions from Semrush Holdings, Inc.'). In the Q2 FY26 release (2026-06-11) the target is STILL 10.2% but now 'factor[s] in the acquisition of Semrush', which contributed ~$480M of ending ARR (~1.9pp). The organic FY26 ARR growth target was therefore cut ~10.2% -> ~8.3%, a ~19% reduction in organic net-new ARR dollars, and was never stated as a cut. The headline instead reads 'Adobe Raises FY26 Total Revenue and Non-GAAP EPS Targets'. Both raises are largely mechanical: the $550M revenue raise is ~$290-300M Semrush plus a ~2pt FX tailwind (13% reported vs 11% constant currency).
corroborating: ARR denominator revalued +$460M ($25.20B -> $25.66B 'entering FY2026', FX) without restating the target's base - see top unverifiable
RPO growth rate dropped: headlined as '+13% y/y' in Q1 FY26, stated as a bare level ($22.27B) with no growth rate in Q2 FY26, and the level is BELOW FY25 year-end $22.52B while now including Semrush
Segment reporting collapsed to ONE reportable segment in Q1 FY26, retiring Digital Media ARR - the decade-tracked metric - in the same quarter the CEO announced departure
GAAP did not participate in the raise: non-GAAP FY26 EPS +$1.00 while GAAP midpoint went $18.00 -> $17.95; the non-GAAP-to-GAAP gap widened to $6.45 = 26% of non-GAAP EPS
~6.6 of the ~16.6 points of FY26 non-GAAP EPS growth come from the share count alone (427M -> ~399M), so 'EPS +17%' overstates business growth
honesty_finding.fairness_note: This is framing, not misstatement. Segment aggregation is ASC 280-permissible, customer-group revenue is still disclosed at two-group granularity, and every underlying datum ($480M Semrush ARR, the $460M revaluation, the GAAP guide) was disclosed. The finding does not make the business worse than the market thinks - the market has marked the leading indicator down harder than Adobe has. It makes management's guidance less trustworthy as a forward guide, which is a reason to underwrite the tape and the revisions rather than the guide.

edge_explainer: Not a claim that the market is wrong about Adobe's business - it is a claim that the market is pricing a ~6% chance the name ever works while the sell-side numbers are at 12-month highs with zero downward revisions. Three things carry it. (1) The de-rate/derailment test resolves cleanly for de-rate on hard revision data: FY26 consensus EPS $23.54 -> $24.41 and FY27 $26.38 -> $27.49 over 90 days, 28-29 up-revisions, zero down, while the multiple collapsed from ~28x to 9.2x - the HUBS/CTSH/SAP signature. (2) The cash-return engine is verified rather than promised: $26.78B of authority (26.7% of the cap), 16.6M shares retired in H1 FY26 at an average price below today's, share count 441M -> 399M over 18 months, on a clean cap structure with no preferred, warrants or converts. (3) The portfolio reason outranks the standalone one - with the household already ~$5.2M/26% long the AI-capex cycle holding, ADBE's bear case REQUIRES that cycle to hold, making it a structurally scarce fundamental offset to the book's largest concentrated risk. Against all that: the organic ARR guidance cut masked by the Semrush acquisition is a genuine takeaway-vs-data divergence and a legitimate partial explanation for the discount, the C-suite has been leaderless for five months with a near-failed say-on-pay, and the path is late at +32.5% off a 46-day-old low. Hence 5/10, 0.65%, staged below spot, with the ARR-denominator gap to be resolved before the second tranche funds.
